acceptance.criterion_verbatim: RULE-24 STATEMENT: axis intent + grain + state-coherence declared in the deliverable.
acceptance.output_evidence: RULE-24 STATEMENT FOR THE LIFECYCLE AXIS (HS-3), stated because a schema act requires it. AXIS + INTENT: ONE axis, the ledger's LIFECYCLE state. It does NOT encode disposition, severity or ownership; those are separate axes and mixing any of them here would break the schema foundationally (24-iii). DECLARED DOMAIN: every sentinel ledger in STATE_DIR. VALUES, MECE over that domain (24-i): OPEN (work outstanding) | HELD (deliberate, gated, well-formed) | terminal (CLOSED/ROLLBACK/SUPERSEDED/...). Mutually exclusive -- a ledger is in exactly one -- and collectively exhaustive, with HELD reachable ONLY through the structural guardrails, never by asserting a status string. SAME GRAIN (24-ii): all three are LEDGER-level. HELD-PAST-REREAD and HELD-STALE are deliberately NOT values on this axis -- they are RE-SURFACE CONDITIONS of HELD, reported as their own finding classes. Putting them on the lifecycle axis would place a staleness OBSERVATION beside a STATE: two grains in one enum. STATE COHERENCE (24-iv): the three values move under DIFFERENT remedies, and that is the whole point of the axis. OPEN clears by DOING THE WORK. HELD clears by THE NAMED GATE MOVING, which is by construction not the ledger owner's act. Terminal moves under nothing. ONE REMEDY DOES NOT MOVE THEM TOGETHER -- which is precisely why a detector that cannot tell a hold from neglect manufactures the wrong reflex, and why HELD had to become checkable rather than claimable. The same statement is carried IN-SOURCE at the constants block so the next editor of the enum meets it where they work, not only in a deliverable they may never open -- a protection that exists only as a description is not a protection.
acceptance.denominator: 4 of 4 postulates addressed (MECE over a named domain, same grain, intent coherence, state coherence); 3 values on the axis; 2 non-values named as such
